title: Standard form
examples: How do I make a very big number into standard form?
What do I do when I multiply numbers in standard form?
Is it always easy to add numbers in standard form?

explain.say: Today we learn about standard form for numbers. It is a neat way to write very large or very small numbers. We use powers of ten to write them down.
To convert a number, we move the decimal point. The number of places you move it tells you the power of ten. For example, two point five times ten to the one is twenty point five.

When multiplying in standard form, we multiply the numbers first. Then we add the powers of ten together. Try one point five times ten to the two times three times ten to the three. The answer is forty five times ten to the five.

Dividing in standard form is similar. We divide the front numbers together. Then we subtract the powers of ten. Consider six point two times ten to the seven divided by two point four times ten to the four. The answer is two point five times ten to the three.

Adding numbers in standard form needs adjustment. The powers of ten must match first. For instance, six point two times ten to the five plus eight point one times ten to the five equals fourteen point three times ten to the five. We adjust the second number first.

faq.q: What is standard form really used for?
faq.a: It helps us write extremely large or small numbers easily. Scientists and engineers use it often in their work. It keeps the numbers neat and manageable.
asks: How do I write big numbers in standard form?
What is the purpose of scientific notation?

faq.q: When I multiply, do I add the powers of ten?
faq.a: Yes, when multiplying, you multiply the front numbers and add the exponents. Remember to keep the answer in standard form format. This keeps your calculation correct.
asks: What do I do with the powers when I multiply?

faq.q: If the powers of ten are different when adding, what should I do?
faq.a: You must adjust the number with the smaller power of ten. You rewrite it so it has the larger power of ten. Then you can add the front numbers normally.
asks: How do I add numbers with different powers?

faq.q: Can I use standard form for decimals?
faq.a: Yes, you can use it for very small numbers too. If the decimal point moves many places to the left, the power of ten will be negative. For example, zero point zero five is five times ten to the negative two.

faq.q: What if the answer after multiplying is bigger than ten?
faq.a: If the front number is ten or more, you must adjust it. You move the decimal point and increase the power of ten. For example, ten times ten to the three is one times ten to the four.
asks: Fixing the front number after multiplication

facts: Standard form uses the structure a times ten to the power of n. The value of a must be between one and ten.
When multiplying numbers in standard form, you multiply the front parts and add the powers of ten.
When dividing numbers in standard form, you divide the front parts and subtract the powers of ten.
When adding or subtracting, the powers of ten must match before you can combine the front parts.

quiz.why: You moved the decimal point six places to the left, so the power is six.

wrong.1: This is tempting because you might count the zeros as six places.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the front number must be less than ten.
wrong.3: This is too large a power of ten for this number.

quiz.why: You multiply four by two to get eight, and you add the powers three plus five to get eight.

wrong.1: This mistake happens when you add the powers instead of multiplying them.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you forgot to add the two separate powers of ten together.
wrong.3: This might happen if you incorrectly added the front numbers four plus two.

quiz.say: What is the result of (9 x 10^6) plus (1 x 10^5)?
quiz.why: You must adjust the first number to have ten to the fifth power first, making it nine hundred times ten to the fifth power.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you added the front numbers but forgot to adjust the powers.
wrong.1: This mistake comes from simply adding the front numbers without adjusting the powers.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you only adjusted one of the numbers, not both.
